## 7. Decision: SPLINE (2026-07-10 — SUPERSEDES §3, §4, §5, §6 recommendation)

> Joey picked Spline as the Refract platform. Additive — §1–§6 stay as historical record and reappear if a shader ever needs work that only R3F can host, but from this point forward the **home** for Refract is Spline. Do NOT recommend other engines. Execute Spline-first.

### 7.1 Rationale (why Spline satisfies "visibility + control to design")
- **Visual editor Joey drives directly** — drag, snap, style, animate in a browser canvas; no HTML surgery, no agent-only opaque edits. Matches the stated prime directive ("see and control every change") without requiring Cursor at all.
- **Shelf/save/reuse built in** — Spline projects, scenes, and components live in his account (`my.spline.design/files`), remixable, versioned, shareable via public/embed URLs.
- **Web now + mobile soon** — Spline exports as (a) a `spline-viewer` web component for any HTML/React/Vue/Svelte site, (b) `@splinetool/runtime` for full JS control, (c) `@splinetool/react-spline` for React Native / Expo (mobile parity), (d) a static image / video / GLB fallback. Same source file feeds all four surfaces.
- **Games AND apps** — Spline supports events, states, variables, physics, and code binding via runtime; sufficient for the configurator app, the watch preview, and small interactive experiences.
- **Prior work already exists** — Joey has a Spline account (joey.walter12@gmail.com) with prior watch scenes; agents have already scraped/interacted with the editor (`spline_browse.mjs`, `spline_intercept.mjs`, `spline_scraper.mjs`, `spline_full.py`, `cdp_direct.py`) and there is a working browser-designer workflow (`~/.gemini/antigravity/brain/…/spline_browser_designer.md`).

### 7.2 Reality check on prior Spline artifacts in this repo
- `MOBILE/assets/scene.splinecode` = **BROKEN. 111 bytes of AWS `AccessDenied` XML** — the failed output of `seize_asset.js` trying to fetch `https://prod.spline.design/ATIn6K-Z2I286-3Y/scene.splinecode` directly from Spline's CDN (Spline blocks unauthenticated origin fetches). Do NOT reference this file in any new build. Leave it in place (additive doctrine) but treat it as archival; the new export lives beside it as `scene.v2.splinecode` when it lands.
- **Public scene IDs referenced by prior configurator versions** (kept as candidate remixes):
  - `ATIn6K-Z2I286-3Y` — "industrial watch" target (403's on direct fetch; needs proper export via editor).
  - `6Wq1Q7YQZxr6h-7h` — used in v15/v16/v17 configurator via `spline-viewer` URL.
  - `K9R7iYj3tQ-9hFmU` — used in v18 configurator via `@splinetool/runtime`.
- **Community scenes previously targeted** for remix (from `spline_intercept.mjs`):
  - `3D Smart Watch` → `f47f17dd-c2a4-44ba-b02b-4a2cc3c25d63`
  - `smart watch` → `251bf8f2-a8f3-4248-9aae-7e286a659c67`
  - `Tech Smart Watch` → `50e6cd06-48a2-4bdd-85e5-a7ae8c6da080`
- **Configurator versions v15–v24** already load Spline correctly via either `<spline-viewer url=…>` or `@splinetool/runtime` `spline.load(…)`. Those loaders are the proven wire; the missing piece was always **a real, exported scene URL**, not the code.

### 7.3 Division of labor (locked)
- **Joey (in Spline editor):** authors the watch scene — case geometry, materials, lighting, camera, states, animations, exposed variables. Owns the shelf. Approves each version.
- **Agents (in this repo):** never mutate Spline scenes. Only assemble the surrounding shell: HTML/React embed, importmap, runtime wire, event/variable bindings to app state, mobile packaging, deploy. Every scene reference is by public URL or by a copied `.splinecode` file dropped into `MOBILE/assets/` by Joey via the Spline "Export → Code (Public URL / Download)" flow.
- **Rule:** never mutate an original scene. Always **Duplicate** first, edit the duplicate. Original scene URLs stay stable so old builds keep rendering.

### 7.4 Shader engine → Spline migration path (all 8 engines from §2)
Spline is not a GLSL engine host; it is a materials + lighting + geometry authoring tool. The 8 fragment engines survive via one of three concrete paths — pick per engine.

| # | Engine (from §2) | Path in Spline | Concrete method |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Named catalog gen-1 (`SHADERS[]`, 80 faces, 3D-noise) | **(b) Baked texture** | Render each named face offscreen in a headless three.js/R3F preview at 1024² or 2048² → PNG/JPG → drop into Spline as an **Image texture** on a `Plane` mesh parented to the watch face. Live-driven texture (video/canvas) also supported via `Video` layer if animation matters. |
| 2 | Named catalog gen-2 (evolved 80-face) | **(b) Baked texture** | Same as engine 1. Same pipeline can batch-render both catalogs from the existing GLSL. |
| 3 | Single field shader (object form) | **(a) Spline material** | Recreate the noise-driven glow as a **Spline "Noise" material** with Fresnel and Emissive on a `Sphere` — visually equivalent, editable inside Spline. |
| 4 | FIELD SHADER DPR-aware (`FRAG`) | **(a) Spline material** | Same as engine 3; DPR handling is unnecessary inside Spline (the runtime handles it). |
| 5 | uMode multi-engine early | **(b) Baked texture, one per mode** | 14 pre-baked textures selectable via a Spline **Variable** driving a "material switch" state. |
| 6 | uMode 14-branch (dots/metaball/lava/smoke/rings/matrix/strings/galaxy/gold/wire/iso/parallax/accretion/starfield) | **(b) Baked texture, one per branch** | Bake all 14 branches from `REFRACT_MASTER_v14.html`'s `FRAG` at 1024²; drop each into Spline as a selectable "Face Design" state variable. Runtime can swap materials on state change. |
| 7 | FRAG2 v15 ENGINE per-design (62 SPECS designs) | **(b) Baked texture, batch of 62** | Batch-render the 62 SPECS entries via a small Node script that runs the same GLSL headless. Each becomes a Spline material preset in a Face Design library. |
| 8 | Liquid raymarch OLED (`LIQ_FRAG`, SDF metaball) | **(c) React-Spline embed + custom GLSL layer** | Liquid raymarch is animated + reflective — baking loses it. Keep it as a live GLSL layer inside an `@splinetool/react-spline` mount: the Spline scene renders the watch body/case/lighting, a transparent WebGL overlay renders the liquid face. Compose via CSS `mix-blend-mode` or a shared canvas. This is the only engine that must stay live-GLSL. |

**Baker script location (to be written next pass):** `MOBILE/tools/bake_faces_v1.mjs` — headless-Chromium or `node-canvas` renderer that walks `SPECS[]` + `SHADERS[]` and writes `MOBILE/assets/faces/<name>.png`. Never mutates originals. Additive.

### 7.5 Asset inventory to hand to Spline
- `MOBILE/assets/chronograph.glb` (7 MB) — **import into Spline** as the watch body via **Assets → Import → 3D Model (GLB/GLTF)**. Use as the base geometry; do not reproduce the case procedurally.
- `MOBILE/assets/studio.hdr` — **import as Environment/HDRI** via Spline Scene Settings → Environment → HDRI upload.
- `MOBILE/assets/wrist.png` — **import as background/plane texture** for the wrist-on preview scene.
- `MOBILE/assets/scene.splinecode` — **DO NOT USE.** Broken (see §7.2).
- Baked face textures (once §7.4 baker runs) — imported per-face as material presets.

### 7.6 Public scene identity for the new Refract build
- Container project: `Refract` (Joey's account, `joey.walter12@gmail.com`).
- Scene 1: `Refract – Watch (v1)` — remix/duplicate of one of the community IDs in §7.2 OR fresh from `chronograph.glb`.
- Scene 2: `Refract – Configurator` — same watch, camera-locked orbit, exposed variables for face-design + material + case-color.
- Scene 3: `Refract – Wrist Preview` — watch on `wrist.png` plate; used for hero shot in the app.
- Every scene has **Export → Public URL** enabled → embed URL of shape `https://prod.spline.design/<publicId>/scene.splinecode`. Those URLs are the single source of truth for the app shell.

### 7.7 App shell wire (already proven in v15/v18/v21/v24 configurators)
Two options, both work, keep both:

**Web component (fastest, zero JS):**
```html
<script type="module" src="https://unpkg.com/@splinetool/viewer@1.9.28/build/spline-viewer.js"></script>
<spline-viewer url="https://prod.spline.design/<publicId>/scene.splinecode"></spline-viewer>
```

**Runtime (full control — read/write variables, listen for events):**
```html
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": { "@splinetool/runtime": "https://unpkg.com/@splinetool/runtime@1.9.28/build/runtime.js" } }
</script>
<script type="module">
  import { Application } from '@splinetool/runtime';
  const app = new Application(document.getElementById('canvas3d'));
  await app.load('https://prod.spline.design/<publicId>/scene.splinecode');
  app.setVariable('faceDesign', 'liquid');
  app.addEventListener('mouseDown', e => { /* … */ });
</script>
```

Mobile (Expo/React Native): `npm i @splinetool/react-spline` and `<Spline scene="https://prod.spline.design/<publicId>/scene.splinecode" />` inside `App_v<N+1>.js`. Same URL, same variables.

### 7.8 First build target — `REFRACT_MASTER_v20.html`
- Copy `REFRACT_MASTER_v19.html` → `v20`. Additive — v19 stays intact.
- Replace the current `<canvas>` + all Three.js face-render init with the runtime-mode block from §7.7 (canvas id `canvas3d` already exists).
- Wire the existing face-picker UI to `app.setVariable('faceDesign', <name>)`.
- Wire the existing color-swatch UI to `app.setVariable('caseColor', <hex>)`.
- Keep the 8-engine face catalog as-is on the JS side — Spline handles the render, JS just tells Spline which state to show.
- Boot bar, intro wordmark, edit-mode panel stay unchanged.
- Success criterion: the Spline watch renders full-screen, face swaps on face-picker click, case color swaps on swatch click, on real Android via Expo.

### 7.9 Hard rules going forward
- Do **NOT** recommend other engines. Spline is the platform. If a use case truly cannot fit Spline (only §7.4 engine 8 so far), attach a small live-GLSL overlay per §7.4 route (c) — don't switch platforms.
- Do **NOT** mutate originals. Every scene edit = duplicate first, edit duplicate, publish new URL.
- Do **NOT** use `MOBILE/assets/scene.splinecode` — it is the broken S3 payload, not a real scene.
- Do **NOT** delete any HTML/JS from `MOBILE/`. Configurator v15–v24 stay as reference for the working Spline wire.
- Do **NOT** author scenes from agents. Agents can inspect, duplicate, and embed; Joey drives the design surface.
